summary: The note surveys the eco-art movement, in which artists use sculpture, painting, digital media and community projects to address climate change, pollution and resource depletion. It profiles many artists and their projects, covering collaboration with scientists, urban nature, technology, sustainable materials, community and school engagement, indigenous wisdom, and economic critique. It concludes that eco-art is gaining momentum as a transformative cultural force for sustainability.
one_line: Overview of eco-artists and their projects that use art, science, technology and community engagement to confront environmental crises.
key_facts: Emma Zhao unveiled the immersive installation "Oceans in Motion" on October 12, 2023, made with marine biologists, visualizing ocean currents and plastic pollution patterns.
Johnathan Watts is a sculptor known for kinetic wind sculptures that double as functional wind turbines contributing to the energy grid, made with renewable energy experts.
On September 20, 2023, Mia Foster transformed a downtown parking lot into a temporary meadow of native wildflowers and grasses titled "Urban Bloom."
Leo Sanchez's virtual reality project "Forests of the Future" launched on November 15, 2023, showing how climate scenarios could alter forests.
Sarah Gibson's installation "Cycle of Life" is made entirely from upcycled industrial waste and found objects, using non-toxic, locally sourced materials.

Max Richter's community mural project, initiated December 4, 2023, had local volunteers paint a mural along the riverbank in his hometown about the river's ecological importance and vulnerability to pollution.
The "Art for Earth" festival kicked off internationally on January 21, 2024, showcasing eco-artists from over 40 countries.
Gabriela Torres began "Roots of Wisdom" in February 2024, collaborating with indigenous communities to combine ancient wisdom and contemporary environmentalism.
Derek Yung, a financial analyst turned artist, started the series "Price Tag Planet" in March 2024, with installations depicting price tags on natural landscapes.
Lily Chang's "Garden of Tomorrow" is an interactive community garden where people plant endemic plants, attend workshops and share stories about environmental stewardship.
Rachel Stevens' "Green Canvas" program, initiated in the past September, integrates eco-art into school curriculums through hands-on projects.
As of September 2023, the note says "eco-art" is no longer a niche interest but at the forefront of cultural discourse.
